explicit_axis_timing.basis: The Constitution's federal government began operating on March 4, 1789; the national government and its commerce and taxation powers were the discrete institutional change coded.
The Constitution's commerce authority took effect with the new federal government in 1789.
Congress authorized the federal funding and debt-assumption plan in 1790.
The First Bank charter was signed on February 25, 1791.
Congress passed the Embargo Act on 22 December 1807.
Congress declared war in June 1812, initiating the major federal wartime mobilization.
Congress chartered the Second Bank of the United States in 1816.
The Supreme Court issued its Dred Scott decision on March 6, 1857.
The Homestead Act was signed on 1862-05-20 and the Pacific Railway Act on 1862-07-01; both authorized federal land transfers, and the railway act also authorized bond support.
The 1863 National Currency Act created the OCC and national charters; the National Banking Act of 1864 established the durable capital and reserve requirements summarized here.
The Thirteenth Amendment was ratified on 1865-12-06.
The Fourteenth Amendment was ratified on 1868-07-09.
The Fifteenth Amendment was ratified on 1870-02-03.
The Third Enforcement Act, commonly called the Ku Klux Klan Act, was enacted on 1871-04-20.
The Interstate Commerce Act became law on 1887-02-04 and created the Interstate Commerce Commission.
The Sherman Anti-Trust Act was approved on 1890-07-02; this codes its enactment, not later trust-busting effectiveness.
The Hepburn Act became law on 1906-06-29 and the Food and Drugs Act on 1906-06-30; these are the first coded sectoral-oversight decisions in this movement.
The Sixteenth Amendment was ratified on 1913-02-03 and the Revenue Act enacted the graduated federal income tax on 1913-10-03.

The Federal Reserve Act was signed on 1913-12-23; this codes institutional creation relative to Treasury-centered crisis management, not full operational independence (which remained limited until the 1951 accord).
The Federal Reserve Act was signed on 1913-12-23 and created the permanent national reserve and supervision architecture.
The FTC Act was signed on 1914-09-26 and the Clayton Act on 1914-10-15; this is the documented competition package underlying this movement summary.
Congress authorized a major naval expansion in 1940, including the Naval Expansion Act and the Two-Ocean Navy program enacted that summer.
The Emergency Price Control Act was enacted on 1942-01-30 and civilian rationing was administered nationally during the war.
Executive Order 9024 established the War Production Board on 1942-01-16 to direct war procurement and production.
The Servicemen's Readjustment Act was signed on 1944-06-22 and authorized veteran education, unemployment, and housing assistance.
The Labor-Management Relations Act was enacted on 1947-06-23; this codes statutory changes, not their measured labor-market effects.
The Treasury and Federal Reserve announced their agreement on 1951-03-04.
The Federal-Aid Highway Act was signed on 1956-06-29, authorizing major federal participation in a national interstate system.
The National Defense Education Act was signed on 1958-09-02.
Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act signed 21 July 2010 (P.L. 111-203).
Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief, and Consumer Protection Act enacted 24 May 2018 (P.L. 115-174).
Section 232 steel and aluminum proclamations and Section 301 China tariff actions began in 2018.
CARES Act signed 27 March 2020 (P.L. 116-136); the dominant cited fiscal expansion was in 2020.
